docs.title: CloudFS
docs.text:
Cloud storage that works like your local filesystem.

CloudFS gives you a pathlib.Path-compatible interface for Google Cloud Storage, AWS S3, and Azure Blob Storage — so you can read, write, list, and move files across cloud providers using the same API you already know.

from cloudfs import Path

p = Path("gs://my-bucket/data/report.csv")
text = p.read_text()

for f in p.parent.iterdir():
    print(f.name)

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• pathlib.Path-compatible API — no new interface to learn
  • Supports Google Cloud Storage, AWS S3, and Azure Blob Storage
  • Single Path() entry point — URI scheme selects the backend automatically
  • isinstance(p, Path) works as expected

docs.title: Supported Backends
docs.text:
Backend URI Scheme Install Google Cloud Storage gs://bucket/key pip install "cloudfs[google]" AWS S3 s3://bucket/key pip install "cloudfs[s3]" Azure Blob Storage az://container/blob pip install "cloudfs[azure]"

Get started →

docs.title: Path(uri)
docs.text:
Entry point. Returns a backend-specific path object based on the URI scheme.

from cloudfs import Path

p = Path("gs://bucket/key")    # → GCSPath
p = Path("s3://bucket/key")    # → S3Path
p = Path("az://container/key") # → AzurePath

isinstance(p, Path) returns True for all backends.

Raises ValueError for unsupported URI schemes.

docs.title: name → str
docs.text:
The final component of the path.

Path("gs://bucket/a/b/report.csv").name  # "report.csv"

docs.title: stem → str
docs.text:
The final component without its suffix.

Path("gs://bucket/a/report.csv").stem  # "report"

docs.title: suffix → str
docs.text:
The file extension of the final component.

Path("gs://bucket/a/report.csv").suffix  # ".csv"

docs.title: suffixes → list[str]
docs.text:
All extensions of the final component.

Path("gs://bucket/a/archive.tar.gz").suffixes  # [".tar", ".gz"]

docs.title: parent → Path
docs.text:
The logical parent of the path.

Path("gs://bucket/a/b/c.txt").parent  # gs://bucket/a/b

docs.title: parents → list[Path]
docs.text: All logical ancestors.

docs.title: parts → tuple[str, ...]
docs.text:
The path split into components. The first element includes the URI scheme and bucket/container.

Path("gs://bucket/a/b.txt").parts  # ("gs://bucket/", "a", "b.txt")

docs.title: drive → str
docs.text:
The URI scheme and bucket/container name.

Path("gs://bucket/key").drive  # "gs://bucket"

docs.title: root → str
docs.text: Always "/".

docs.title: anchor → str
docs.text:
drive + root.

Path("gs://bucket/key").anchor  # "gs://bucket/"

docs.title: path / other → Path
docs.text:
Join paths using the / operator.

p = Path("gs://bucket/data") / "2024" / "report.csv"

docs.title: joinpath(*others) → Path
docs.text: Equivalent to chaining /.

docs.title: with_name(name) → Path
docs.text:
Return a new path with the filename changed.

Path("gs://bucket/a/old.txt").with_name("new.txt")  # gs://bucket/a/new.txt

docs.title: with_stem(stem) → Path
docs.text: Return a new path with the stem changed, preserving the suffix.

docs.title: with_suffix(suffix) → Path
docs.text:
Return a new path with the suffix changed.

Path("gs://bucket/a/report.txt").with_suffix(".csv")  # gs://bucket/a/report.csv

docs.title: is_absolute() → bool
docs.text: Always True — cloud paths are always absolute.

docs.title: resolve(strict=False) → Path
docs.text: Returns a new path object equal to self (cloud paths are already absolute).

docs.title: absolute() → Path
docs.text: Same as resolve().

docs.title: exists() → bool
docs.text: True if the path refers to an existing file or directory.

docs.title: is_file() → bool
docs.text: True if the path is an existing file (blob/object).

docs.title: is_dir() → bool
docs.text: True if the path is a directory (has children or a placeholder blob).

docs.title: samefile(other) → bool
docs.text: True if both paths point to the same object in the same bucket/container.

docs.title: iterdir() → Iterator[Path]
docs.text: Yield the direct children of a directory (one level only).

docs.title: glob(pattern) → Iterator[Path]
docs.text:
Yield all matching paths using shell-style pattern matching.

for f in Path("gs://bucket/data/").glob("*.csv"):
    print(f)

docs.title: rglob(pattern) → Iterator[Path]
docs.text: Like glob() but recursive.

docs.title: walk(top_down=True, on_error=None) → Generator
docs.text: Yield (dirpath, dirnames, filenames) tuples, similar to os.walk().

docs.title: open(mode='r', encoding=None, errors=None, newline=None) → IO
docs.text:
Open the file. Supports modes 'r', 'rb', 'w', 'wb'.

with p.open("r") as f:
    print(f.read())

docs.title: read_bytes() → bytes
docs.text: Return the full contents as bytes.

docs.title: read_text(encoding='utf-8') → str
docs.text: Return the full contents as a string.

docs.title: write_bytes(data: bytes) → int
docs.text: Write bytes and return the number of bytes written.

docs.title: write_text(data: str, encoding='utf-8') → int
docs.text: Write text and return the number of bytes written.

docs.title: touch(mode=0o666, exist_ok=True) → None
docs.text: Create the file if it does not exist. If exist_ok=False, raises FileExistsError when the file already exists.

docs.title: unlink(missing_ok=False) → None
docs.text: Delete the file. Raises FileNotFoundError if the file does not exist and missing_ok=False.

docs.title: rename(target) → Path
docs.text: Move the file to target and return the new path.

docs.title: replace(target) → Path
docs.text: Alias for rename().

docs.title: mkdir(parents=False, exist_ok=False) → None
docs.text: Create a directory placeholder. Raises FileExistsError if it already exists and exist_ok=False.

docs.title: rmdir() → None
docs.text: Delete a directory placeholder created by mkdir(). Raises FileNotFoundError if the placeholder does not exist, and OSError if the directory is not empty.

docs.title: stat(follow_symlinks=True) → StatResult
docs.text:
Return an object with:

Attribute Type Description st_size int Size in bytes st_mtime float Last modified (Unix timestamp) st_ctime float Created time (Unix timestamp); falls back to st_mtime on backends that don't track creation time

docs.title: CloudOperationError
docs.text:
Raised when a pathlib.Path operation has no meaningful cloud equivalent.

from cloudfs import CloudOperationError

Operations that always raise CloudOperationError:

  • is_symlink(), symlink_to(), hardlink_to()
  • is_mount(), is_junction()
  • is_block_device(), is_char_device(), is_fifo(), is_socket()
  • lstat(), chmod(), lchmod()
  • relative_to(), is_relative_to()
  • expanduser(), home(), cwd()

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Install CloudFS with the backend(s) you need:

# Google Cloud Storage
pip install "cloudfs[google]"

# AWS S3
pip install "cloudfs[s3]"

# Azure Blob Storage
pip install "cloudfs[azure]"

# All backends
pip install "cloudfs[all]"

docs.title: Credentials
docs.text:
CloudFS uses each provider's standard credential mechanism — no extra configuration needed.

Google Cloud Storage

Set the path to your service account key:

export GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS=/path/to/key.json

Or use Application Default Credentials via gcloud auth application-default login.

AWS S3

Set your access key in environment variables:

export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=...
export AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=...
export AWS_DEFAULT_REGION=ap-northeast-1

Or configure via aws configure if you have the AWS CLI installed.

Azure Blob Storage

Set your connection string:

export AZURE_STORAGE_CONNECTION_STRING="DefaultEndpointsProtocol=https;AccountName=...;AccountKey=...;EndpointSuffix=core.windows.net"

Find it in: Azure Portal → Storage Account → Access keys → Connection string.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
Create a Path by passing any supported URI — the backend is selected automatically:

from cloudfs import Path

# Google Cloud Storage
p = Path("gs://my-bucket/data/hello.txt")

# AWS S3
p = Path("s3://my-bucket/data/hello.txt")

# Azure Blob Storage
p = Path("az://my-container/data/hello.txt")

docs.title: Read & Write
docs.text:
from cloudfs import Path

p = Path("gs://my-bucket/notes/hello.txt")

# Write
p.write_text("Hello, CloudFS!")

# Read
print(p.read_text())  # Hello, CloudFS!

# Binary
p.write_bytes(b"\x00\x01\x02")
data = p.read_bytes()

docs.title: Navigate
docs.text:
p = Path("gs://my-bucket/data/2024/report.csv")

print(p.name)    # report.csv
print(p.stem)    # report
print(p.suffix)  # .csv
print(p.parent)  # gs://my-bucket/data/2024

# Join paths
p2 = p.parent / "summary.csv"
print(p2)        # gs://my-bucket/data/2024/summary.csv

docs.title: List & Glob
docs.text:
base = Path("gs://my-bucket/data/")

# List direct children
for child in base.iterdir():
    print(child)

# Glob
for csv in base.glob("*.csv"):
    print(csv)

# Walk recursively
for dirpath, dirnames, filenames in base.walk():
    for f in filenames:
        print(dirpath / f)

docs.title: File operations
docs.text:
p = Path("gs://my-bucket/tmp/file.txt")

p.touch()                     # create empty file
p.exists()                    # True
p.is_file()                   # True
p.unlink()                    # delete
p.unlink(missing_ok=True)     # delete, no error if missing

p.rename(p.with_name("new.txt"))   # move

docs.title: URI Format
docs.text: az://container-name/path/to/blob

docs.title: Credentials
docs.text:
Set the connection string from your storage account:

export AZURE_STORAGE_CONNECTION_STRING="DefaultEndpointsProtocol=https;AccountName=...;AccountKey=...;EndpointSuffix=core.windows.net"

Find it in: Azure Portal → Storage Account → Access keys → Connection string.

Ensure Allow storage account key access is enabled under Settings → Configuration, and that Public network access is set to Enabled from all networks (or your IP is allowlisted).

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
from cloudfs import Path

p = Path("az://my-container/data/report.csv")
p.write_text("hello")
print(p.read_text())

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
Directories are virtual. Azure Blob Storage has no real directories — only blob names containing slashes.

  • mkdir() creates a zero-byte placeholder blob (prefix/). If you delete all files under a directory but the placeholder remains, is_dir() still returns True.
  • Writing directly to a sub-path never requires a prior mkdir().
  • A path can simultaneously satisfy is_file() and is_dir() if a blob named foo and another named foo/bar both exist.

rmdir() only removes placeholder blobs. A "virtual" directory that was never explicitly created via mkdir() will raise FileNotFoundError from rmdir() even if is_dir() returns True.

rename() is not atomic. It is implemented as copy + delete. A crash between the two steps leaves both source and destination in place.

open() buffers in memory. Read modes download the full blob; write modes buffer and upload on close().

Performance. Each exists(), is_file(), and is_dir() call makes at least one API request. Prefer iterdir() or walk() for bulk operations.

docs.title: URI Format
docs.text: gs://bucket-name/path/to/object

docs.title: Credentials
docs.text:
CloudFS uses Application Default Credentials.

Option 1 — Service account key file:

export GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS=/path/to/service-account.json

Option 2 — Application Default Credentials:

gcloud auth application-default login

Required IAM role: Storage Object Admin (or Storage Object Creator + Storage Object Viewer).

docs.text:
Directories are virtual. GCS has no real directories — only object names containing slashes.

  • mkdir() creates a zero-byte placeholder object (prefix/). If you delete all files under a directory but the placeholder remains, is_dir() still returns True.
  • Writing directly to a sub-path never requires a prior mkdir().
  • A path can simultaneously satisfy is_file() and is_dir() if a blob named foo and another named foo/bar both exist.

rmdir() only removes placeholder blobs. A "virtual" directory that was never explicitly created via mkdir() will raise FileNotFoundError from rmdir() even if is_dir() returns True.

Performance. Each exists(), is_file(), and is_dir() call makes at least one API request. Prefer iterdir() or walk() for bulk operations.

docs.title: URI Format
docs.text: s3://bucket-name/path/to/object

docs.title: Credentials
docs.text:
CloudFS uses boto3's credential chain.

Option 1 — Environment variables:

export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=...
export AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=...
export AWS_DEFAULT_REGION=ap-northeast-1

Option 2 — AWS CLI:

aws configure

Required IAM policy: AmazonS3FullAccess (or a scoped policy with s3:GetObject, s3:PutObject, s3:DeleteObject, s3:ListBucket).

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
from cloudfs import Path

p = Path("s3://my-bucket/data/report.csv")
p.write_text("hello")
print(p.read_text())

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
Directories are virtual. S3 has no real directories — only object keys containing slashes.

  • mkdir() creates a zero-byte placeholder object (prefix/). If you delete all files under a directory but the placeholder remains, is_dir() still returns True.
  • Writing directly to a sub-path never requires a prior mkdir().
  • A path can simultaneously satisfy is_file() and is_dir() if an object named foo and another named foo/bar both exist.

rmdir() only removes placeholder objects. A "virtual" directory that was never explicitly created via mkdir() will raise FileNotFoundError from rmdir() even if is_dir() returns True.

open() buffers in memory. S3 has no native streaming file object. Read modes download the full object into memory; write modes buffer in memory and upload on close().

Performance. Each exists(), is_file(), and is_dir() call makes at least one API request. Prefer iterdir() or walk() for bulk operations.
